title: security: rbac v2 & audit: fix missing KMS region pinning in audit logs
description:
Background: When enforcing KMS region pinning alongside RBAC v2, audit records sometimes omitted the kms_key_region field for short-lived key material used by private deployments. This caused false negatives in residency compliance checks and made post-hoc forensics for cross-region access harder.

This PR fixes the audit logging path and RBAC validator to ensure kms_key_region is always captured and validated when region pinning is enabled. It also tightens the RBAC v2 residency enforcement to reject role bindings that specify cross-region KMS keys without an explicit exception.

Summary of changes: - Ensure audit logger surface includes kms_key_region for encrypted secrets and ephemeral key handles. - Add kms region field to the audit schema v2 and migration shim for older records. - Update rbac v2 validator to run residency checks against key region metadata and to emit clear audit entries on rejection. - Add unit and integration tests validating audit entries and policy enforcement. - Docs: update RBAC v2 policy docs to call out KMS region pinning behavior and migration notes.

Checklist: - [x] Add unit tests for kms_key_region extraction and RBAC rule evaluation - [x] Add integration test covering private-installer + audit log end-to-end - [x] Update audit schema v2 and add lightweight migration compatibility shim - [x] Add docs entry in security/rbac-v2.md - [x] Run CI and address failures

Testing: Local unit + integration suite ran. CI initially hit a flaky unit test (timeout on TestKVCachePersistence) which was unrelated; reran the job and all checks passed. Manual validation performed against a staging private deployment with kms region pinning enabled and sample rotation flows.

Migration notes: The audit schema v2 adds an optional string field kms_key_region. We provide a migration shim that backfills region='unknown' for older entries so analytics queries remain stable. No customer-visible downtime.

Motivation/Risk: Regulatory customers rely on reliable region residency signals. This was identified during an internal compliance audit (ENG-3245). The change is low-risk: adds a new optional audit field and tightens existing validator logic. No breaking changes to public API.
